# Ida Ashdown

## Overview

- **Age:** 10 years old  <sub>[v5 c4 P5](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0005)</sub>
- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v5 c4 P5](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0005)</sub>
- **Status:** alive  <sub>[v5 c35 P9](../source/v05-c35.md#nw-v05-c35-p0009)</sub>
- **Origin:** Juneford  <sub>[v5 c4 P58](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0058)</sub>
- **Role:** schoolgirl  <sub>[v5 c4 P58](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0058)</sub>

## Appearance

Ida is a slender, pale girl with dark-blue eyes and limp, pitch-black hair that she wears in plaits. Her features are small, delicate, and pale, with a habit of her lips parting above her minute ivory teeth.

_Sources: [v5 c4 P5](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0005), [v5 c4 P8](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0008), [v5 c14 P18](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0018), [v5 c23 P0](../source/v05-c23.md#nw-v05-c23-p0000)_

## Personality

Ida is a visionary, sensitive, and deeply empathetic girl who possesses a quiet, gentle nature. She is earnest and reflective, often feeling things deeply and harboring a tender, unmothered longing for affection. Though shy, nervous, and easily frightened, she is capable of profound selflessness, courage, and moral devotion for the sake of those she loves.

_Sources: [v5 c4 P5](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0005), [v5 c4 P8](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0008), [v5 c5 P68](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0068), [v5 c5 P84](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0084), [v5 c5 P106](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0106), [v5 c9 P11](../source/v05-c09.md#nw-v05-c09-p0011), [v5 c9 P14](../source/v05-c09.md#nw-v05-c09-p0014), [v5 c34 P18](../source/v05-c34.md#nw-v05-c34-p0018)_

## History

Ida resides at the Glen St. Agnes manse as the daughter of the local Presbyterian minister. After her mother's death, she and her siblings grew up with little supervision, forming a close bond with each other and the Carrow children, frequently playing in Fern Hollow and the local cemetery. When a runaway orphan named Mary Stubbs arrived, Ida showed her great compassion, sharing her bed and advocating for her to be allowed to stay. Ida participated in founding the Good-Conduct Club with her siblings to discipline themselves and spare their father embarrassment. Following a misdeed, she participated in a day-long fast as self-punishment and fainted during a church service from exhaustion. Fearing that their bad behavior would prevent her father from remarrying and finding happiness, Ida bravely visited Clementine Ainslie on her own, overcoming her fear of stepmothers to ask Clementine to marry her father. Her selfless plea moved Clementine, leading to the reconciliation and eventual marriage of her father and Clementine.

_Sources: [v5 c4 P5](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0005), [v5 c4 P45](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0045), [v5 c5 P63](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0063), [v5 c5 P78](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0078), [v5 c5 P84](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0084), [v5 c5 P102](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0102), [v5 c23 P64](../source/v05-c23.md#nw-v05-c23-p0064), [v5 c28 P11](../source/v05-c28.md#nw-v05-c28-p0011), [v5 c28 P19](../source/v05-c28.md#nw-v05-c28-p0019), [v5 c34 P13](../source/v05-c34.md#nw-v05-c34-p0013), [v5 c34 P24](../source/v05-c34.md#nw-v05-c34-p0024), [v5 c34 P36](../source/v05-c34.md#nw-v05-c34-p0036)_
